verses.zh: 撒拉享寿一百二十七岁，这是撒拉一生的岁数。
verses.en: Sarah lived 127 years.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “And the life of Sarah was one hundred years and twenty years and seven years, the years of the life of Sarah.”
verses.commentary:
23:1 Rabbinical Midrash says that when Abraham returned home and told Sarah what he had done, in
response she issued seven loud cries and died. Her death is recorded in chapter 23. Whether this is true or
not, we can certainly see where the rabbis got their interpretation!

▣ "these were the years of the life of Sarah" This phrase is missing in the LXX but present
in the Peshitta. The UBS Text Project, p. 32, suggests it as a later gloss and gives it a "C" rating (considerable
doubt). It suggests that translators omit the secondary phrase (cf. TEV, NJB, Net).

verses.zh: 撒拉死在迦南地的基列・亚巴，就是希伯仑。亚伯拉罕为她哀恸哭号。
verses.en: Then she[NOTE:1] died in Kiriath Arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan. Abraham went to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “Sarah.” The proper name has been replaced in the translation by the pronoun (“she”) for stylistic reasons.

Mourn…weep. The description here is of standard mourning rites (see K. A. Kitchen, NBD3 149-50). They would have been carried out in the presence of the corpse, probably in Sarah’s tent. So Abraham came in to mourn; then he rose up to go and bury his dead (v. 3).
verses.commentary:
23:2 "Kiriath-arba" This name (BDB 900) is made up of

- "Kiriath" means "city"

- "Arba"

- usually translated "city of four" (i.e., Anak and his three sons or four villages together)

- the same root means "ambush" (BDB 70)

- a person's name, one of the Anakim, Jos. 14:15; 15:13; 21:11

SPECIAL TOPIC: GIANTS

▣ "Abraham went in to mourn Sarah and weep for her" One wonders how long this mourning and
the negotiating with the locals lasted. The body of Sarah would deteriorate quickly in this climate (see the
chapter on Death and Funeral Rites" in Ancient Israel: Social Institutions, vol. 1 by Roland deVaux,
pp. 56-61 and SPECIAL
TOPIC: BURIAL PRACTICES). Today in Israel (which still does not embalm) one must be buried within twenty
four hours.

For "Sarah" see
SPECIAL TOPIC: SARAI/SARAH

verses.zh: 后来亚伯拉罕从死人面前起来，对赫人说：
verses.en: Then Abraham got up from mourning his dead wife[NOTE:1] and said to the sons of Heth,[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “And Abraham arose from upon the face of his dead.”

Heb “sons of Heth,” the gentilic of which is הִתִּי (hitti) “Hittites.” Some translations use “Hittites” here (also in vv. 5, 7, 10, 16, 18, 20). But these people were not the classical Hittites of Anatolia (in Asia Minor, modern Turkey). These sons of Heth are apparently a Canaanite group (see Gen 10:15). See H. A. Hoffner, Jr., “Hittites,” Peoples of the Old Testament World 152-53. But cf. also V. Hamilton, Genesis 18-50 (NICOT), 126-128.
verses.commentary:
23:3-13 What follows through the rest of the chapter is a record of the dialogue (using formalized and
standard Oriental customs) between the local inhabitants near Hebron and Abraham. Note the formalities
expressed in IMPERATIVES (note paragraphing of TEV).

- "give me," Gen. 23:4, BDB 678, KB 733, Qal IMPERATIVE in the sense of a
request

- "burial site," Gen. 23:4 (lit. possession for a burying place), BDB 868, KB 1064, Qal
COHORTATIVE

- "hear," Gen. 23:6, BDB 1033, KB 1570, Qal IMPERATIVE (used by the sons of Heth
to Abraham)

- "bury your dead," Gen. 23:6, BDB 868, KB 1064, Qal IMPERATIVE (this was not
what Abraham wanted to do, i.e., bury Sarah on one of their lands)

- "hear," Gen. 23:8, same as #3, but Abraham speaks to them

- "approach" (or entreat), Gen. 23:8, BDB 803, KB 910, Qal IMPERATIVE
(as request)

- "give," Gen. 23:9, BDB 678, KB 733

- Qal JUSSIVE

- Qal IMPERFECT used in a JUSSIVE sense

(Ephron responds in Gen. 23:11 [three Qal PERFECTS],
but this is not a literal offer of a gift of the land, rather part of the expected
negotiations; it basically denotes a pending sale)

- "hear," Gen. 23:11, same as #3 and #5 (Ephron speaks to Abraham and offers the cave and the field)

- "bury," Gen. 23:11, same as #4

- "listen" (lit. "hear"), Gen. 23:13, same as #3,5,8 (Abraham speaks to Ephron)

- "hear," Gen. 23:15, same as #3,5,8,10 (Ephron speaks to Abraham in such a way about the price of
the field that all negotiation over the price is excluded, and this was apparently a high price)

Much of this dialogue seems formal or repetitious to us, but it was the expected protocol of
Canaanite society in the second millennium B.C.

23:3 "the sons of Heth" The name Heth (תח, BDB 366) is an ancestor of the Hittites
(יתח, BDB 366, cf. Gen. 10:15; 1 Chr. 1:13).

SPECIAL
TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

verses.zh: 「我在你们中间是外人，是寄居的。求你们在这里给我一块地，我好埋葬我的死人，使她不在我眼前。」
verses.en: “I am a foreign resident, a temporary settler,[NOTE:1] among you. Grant[NOTE:2] me ownership[NOTE:3] of a burial site among you so that I may[NOTE:4] bury my dead.”[NOTE:5]
notes: Heb “a resident foreigner (גֵּר; ger) and an immigrant (תּוֹשָׁב; toshav).” The term גֵּר (ger) refers to a foreign resident, but with different social implications in different settings. The Patriarchs were foreign, temporary residents in parts of Canaan, who abided by the claims of local authorities (see Gen 20, 23, 26). The noun toshav (תּוֹשָׁב) is less common. Under Mosaic Law it refers to someone of lesser standing than a resident foreigner (גֵּר; ger) since the ger had given full covenantal allegiance to the Lord. While not referring to a citizen, the precise nuance of toshav as an immigrant, resident, or (temporary) settler, is not clear. But in this case it may be a case of hendiadys, where the two terms together mean “an alien resident.”
Heb “give,” which is used here as an idiom for “sell” (see v. 9). The idiom reflects the polite bartering that was done in the culture at the time.
Or “possession.”
Following the imperative, the cohortative with the prefixed conjunction expresses purpose.
Heb “bury my dead out of my sight.” The last phrase “out of my sight” has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
23:4 "a stranger and a sojourner" These two terms have different connotations, but are probably here a
hendiadys.

- "a stranger" (BDB 158) implies an alien resident, cf. Gen. 15:13; Exod. 22:21; 23:9; Lev. 19:34;
Deut. 10:19; 23:8

- "a sojourner" (BDB 444) is an alien just passing through with no legal rights, Lev. 22:10; 25:40

Possibly taken together, they imply someone who moved into an unsettled area, but did not own land.
See article on "Resident Aliens" in Ancient Israel: Social Institutions, vol. 1, by Roland deVaux,
pp. 74-76.

verses.zh: 赫人回答亚伯拉罕说：
verses.en: The sons of Heth answered Abraham,[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “answered Abraham saying to him.”

verses.zh: 「我主请听。你在我们中间是一位尊大的王子，只管在我们最好的坟地里埋葬你的死人；我们没有一人不容你在他的坟地里埋葬你的死人。」
verses.en: “Listen, sir,[NOTE:1] you are a mighty prince[NOTE:2] among us! You may bury your dead in the choicest of our tombs. None of us will refuse you his tomb to prevent you[NOTE:3] from burying your dead.”
notes: Heb “Hear us, my lord.”

Heb “prince of God.” The divine name may be used here as a means of expressing the superlative, “mighty prince.” The word for “prince” probably means “tribal chief” here. See M. H. Gottstein, “Nasiʾ ʾelohim (Gen 23:6),” VT 3 (1953) 298-99; and D. W. Thomas, “Consideration of Some Unusual Ways of Expressing the Superlative in Hebrew,” VT 3 (1953) 215-16.
The phrase “to prevent you” has been added in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
23:6 "you are a mighty prince" The term translated "mighty" is the term elohim (BDB 43), which
can be used of

- God, see SPECIAL TOPIC:
NAMES FOR DEITY

- judges

- angels

- here denoting a powerful, local, family leader

The translation "mighty" comes from the root meaning of el (BDB 42, cf. 1 Chr. 12:22;
Ps. 68:15; Jonah 3:3). Some commentators want to translate it "prince of God."

The term translated "prince" (BDB 672) means "one lifted up" (from basic root, BDB 669). The
NASB translates it as

- "prince" in Gen. 17:20; 25:16; 34:2

- "leader" in Exod. 16:22; Num. 1:16,44; 2:3; Jos. 22:32

- "ruler" in Exod. 22:28; 34:31; 35:27; 1 Kgs. 11:34

- "chief" in Josh 13:21

In this highly stylized negotiation this is a polite title of respect. The Hittites are not making
a religious statement.

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕就起来，向那地的赫人下拜，
verses.en: Abraham got up and bowed down to the local people,[NOTE:1] the sons of Heth.
notes: Heb “to the people of the land” (also in v. 12).

verses.zh: 对他们说：「你们若有意叫我埋葬我的死人，使她不在我眼前，就请听我的话，为我求琐辖的儿子以弗仑，
verses.en: Then he said to them, “If you agree[NOTE:1] that I may bury my dead,[NOTE:2] then hear me out.[NOTE:3] Ask[NOTE:4] Ephron the son of Zohar
notes: Heb “If it is with your purpose.” The Hebrew noun נֶפֶשׁ (nefesh) here has the nuance “purpose” or perhaps “desire” (see BDB 661 s.v. נֶפֶשׁ).
Heb “bury my dead out of my sight.” The last phrase “out of my sight” has not been included in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Or “hear me.”
Heb “intercede for me with.”

verses.zh: 把田头上那麦比拉洞给我，他可以按着足价卖给我，作我在你们中间的坟地。」
verses.en: if he will sell[NOTE:1] me the cave of Machpelah that belongs to him; it is at the end of his field. Let him sell it to me publicly[NOTE:2] for the full price,[NOTE:3] so that I may own it as a burial site.”
notes: Heb “give.” This is used here (also a second time later in this verse) as an idiom for “sell”; see the note on the word “grant” in v. 4.
Heb “in your presence.”
Heb “full silver.”
verses.commentary:
23:9 "the cave of Machpelah" This seems to be a cave (common burial place) located in the district of
Machpelah, an outlying region from Hebron toward Mamre (cf. Gen. 13:18; 14:13; 18:1).

Several of Abraham's family were buried here.

- Sarah, Gen. 23:19

- Abraham, Gen. 25:9

- Isaac, Gen. 35:29

- Rebekah and Leah, Gen. 49:31

- Jacob, Gen. 50:13

verses.zh: 当时以弗仑正坐在赫人中间。于是，赫人以弗仑在城门出入的赫人面前对亚伯拉罕说：
verses.en: (Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth.) Ephron the Hittite[NOTE:1] replied to Abraham in the hearing[NOTE:2] of the sons of Heth—before all who entered the gate[NOTE:3] of his city—
notes: The Hebrew term is “Hittite,” but see the note on the name “Heth” in v. 3.
Heb “ears.” By metonymy the “ears” stand for the presence or proximity (i.e., within earshot) of the persons named.

On the expression all who entered the gate see E. A. Speiser, “‘Coming’ and ‘Going’ at the City Gate,” BASOR 144 (1956): 20-23; and G. Evans, “‘Coming’ and ‘Going’ at the City Gate: A Discussion of Professor Speiser’s Paper,” BASOR 150 (1958): 28-33.
verses.commentary:
23:10 "the Hittite" See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: PRE-ISRAELITE INHABITANTS OF PALESTINE

▣ "at the gate" This would have been the place where local leaders met for fellowship,
commerce, and legal matters.

verses.zh: 「不然，我主请听。我送给你这块田，连田间的洞也送给你，在我同族的人面前都给你，可以埋葬你的死人。」
verses.en: “No, my lord! Hear me out. I sell[NOTE:1] you both the field and the cave that is in it.[NOTE:2] In the presence of my people[NOTE:3] I sell it to you. Bury your dead.”
notes: Heb “give.” The perfect tense has here a present nuance; this is a formal, legally binding declaration. Abraham asked only for a burial site/cave within the field; Ephron agrees to sell him the entire field.
The Hebrew text adds “to you I give [i.e., sell] it.” This is redundant in English and has not been translated for stylistic reasons.
Heb “in the presence of the sons of my people.”

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕就在那地的人民面前下拜，
verses.en: Abraham bowed before the local people

verses.zh: 在他们面前对以弗仑说：「你若应允，请听我的话。我要把田价给你，求你收下，我就在那里埋葬我的死人。」
verses.en: and said to Ephron in their hearing, “Hear me, if you will. I pay[NOTE:1] to you the price[NOTE:2] of the field. Take it from me so that I may[NOTE:3] bury my dead there.”
notes: Heb “give.”
Heb “silver.”
After the imperative, the cohortative with the prefixed conjunction expresses purpose or result.

verses.zh: 以弗仑回答亚伯拉罕说：
verses.en: Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him,

verses.zh: 「我主请听。值四百舍客勒银子的一块田，在你我中间还算甚么呢？只管埋葬你的死人吧！」
verses.en: “Hear me, my lord. The land is worth[NOTE:1] 400 pieces of silver,[NOTE:2] but what is that between me and you? So bury your dead.”
notes: The word “worth” has been supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.

400 pieces of silver. The standards for weighing money varied considerably in the ancient Near East, but the generally accepted weight for the shekel is 11.5 grams (0.4 ounce). This makes the weight of silver here 4.6 kilograms, or 160 ounces (about 10 pounds).
verses.commentary:
23:15 "shekels" See
SPECIAL
TOPIC: ANE WEIGHTS AND VOLUMES

verses.zh: 亚伯拉罕听从了以弗仑，照着他在赫人面前所说的话，把买卖通用的银子平了四百舍客勒给以弗仑。
verses.en: So Abraham agreed to Ephron’s price[NOTE:1] and weighed out[NOTE:2] for him[NOTE:3] the price[NOTE:4] that Ephron had quoted[NOTE:5] in the hearing of the sons of Heth—400 pieces of silver, according to the standard measurement at the time.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “listened to Ephron.”
Heb “and Abraham weighed out.”
Heb “to Ephron.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation for stylistic reasons.
Heb “silver.”
Heb “that he had spoken.” The referent (Ephron) has been specified here in the translation for clarity and for stylistic reasons.
Heb “passing for the merchant.” The final clause affirms that the measurement of silver was according to the standards used by the merchants of the time.

verses.zh: 于是，麦比拉、幔利前、以弗仑的那块田和其中的洞，并田间四围的树木，
verses.en: So Abraham secured[NOTE:1] Ephron’s field in Machpelah, next to Mamre, including the field, the cave that was in it, and all the trees that were in the field and all around its border,
notes: Heb “And it was conveyed.” The recipient, Abraham (mentioned in the Hebrew text at the beginning of v. 18) has been placed here in the translation for stylistic reasons.
verses.commentary:
23:17 "were deeded over" The VERB (BDB 877, KB 1086, Qal IMPERFECT with
waw) means to raise or stand up. It came to refer to legal transactions as being established. Abraham now
officially owned land in Palestine/Canaan. He was no longer a sojourner and alien.

verses.zh: 都定准归与亚伯拉罕，乃是他在赫人面前并城门出入的人面前买妥的。
verses.en: as his property in the presence of the sons of Heth before all who entered the gate of Ephron’s city.[NOTE:1]
notes: Heb “his city”; the referent (Ephron) has been specified in the translation for clarity.sn See G. M. Tucker, “The Legal Background of Genesis 23, ” JBL 85 (1966):77-84; and M. R. Lehmann, “Abraham’s Purchase of Machpelah and Hittite Law,” BASOR 129 (1953): 15-18.

verses.zh: 此后，亚伯拉罕把他妻子撒拉埋葬在迦南地幔利前的麦比拉田间的洞里。（幔利就是希伯仑）。
verses.en: After this Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave in the field of Machpelah next to Mamre (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan.

verses.zh: 从此，那块田和田间的洞就藉着赫人定准归与亚伯拉罕作坟地。
verses.en: So Abraham secured the field and the cave that was in it as a burial site[NOTE:1] from the sons of Heth.
notes: Heb “possession of a grave.”

NASB (UPDATED) TEXT: GENESIS 23:1-16

1Now Sarah lived one hundred and twenty-seven years; these were the years of the life of Sarah. 2Sarah died in Kiriath-arba (that is, Hebron) in the land of Canaan; and Abraham went in to mourn for Sarah and to weep for her. 3Then Abraham rose from before his dead, and spoke to the sons of Heth, saying, 4"I am a stranger and a sojourner among you; give me a burial site among you that I may bury my dead out of my sight." 5The sons of Heth answered Abraham, saying to him, 6"Hear us, my lord, you are a mighty prince among us; bury your dead in the choicest of our graves; none of us will refuse you his grave for burying your dead." 7So Abraham rose and bowed to the people of the land, the sons of Heth. 8And he spoke with them, saying, "If it is your wish for me to bury my dead out of my sight, hear me, and approach Ephron the son of Zohar for me, 9that he may give me the cave of Machpelah which he owns, which is at the end of his field; for the full price let him give it to me in your presence for a burial site." 10Now Ephron was sitting among the sons of Heth; and Ephron the Hittite answered Abraham in the hearing of the sons of Heth; even of all who went in at the gate of his city, saying, 11"No, my lord, hear me; I give you the field, and I give you the cave that is in it. In the presence of the sons of my people I give it to you; bury your dead." 12And Abraham bowed before the people of the land. 13He spoke to Ephron in the hearing of the people of the land, saying, "If you will only please listen to me; I will give the price of the field, accept it from me that I may bury my dead there." 14Then Ephron answered Abraham, saying to him, 15"My lord, listen to me; a piece of land worth four hundred shekels of silver, what is that between me and you? So bury your dead." 16Abraham listened to Ephron; and Abraham weighed out for Ephron the silver which he had named in the hearing of the sons of Heth, four hundred shekels of silver, commercial standard.
